genotype.statement: Homozygous NM_015687.5:c.3398C>T,p.Pro1133Leu matches packet coding/protein/allelic state. S2/S3 use genomic76022150G>A;packet usesGRCh38 NC_000006.12:g.75312434G>A.
limitations: Exact cross-assembly normalization and NP_056502.1 accession not independently established; coding correspondence is explicit. S2 CADD24.2 versusS3 CADD26.9 is retained as source inconsistency.

segregation.statement: Both consanguineous parents are reported carriers and the affected child homozygous.

phase.statement: Reported homozygous variant and carrier mother/father support biparental inheritance; no two distinct variants require cis/trans phasing.

causal_confidence.statement: Authors attribute a recessive congenital myopathy/dysmorphism/neurodevelopmental disorder to FILIP1 variants; packet causal gene/disease is broadly concordant. Pro1133Leu has allele-specific reduced solubility/increased proteolysis and Patient3 muscle/fibroblast observations.
limitations: No formal ACMG classification grid establishes packet PATHOGENIC as a separately documented clinical classification; later OMIM620775 naming is not independently adjudicated.

Five patients/four families; functional evidence is mainly Patient3 and protein fragments. One patient fibroblast line with technical replicates does not supply independent biological patient replication or prove every phenotype causal.

Alternative variants listed in all S3 sheets were fully read; authors did not consider them explanatory, but table annotations alone do not exclude every genetic cause. No raw exome/proteomic reanalysis performed.

limitations: Explicit negatives separated from unreported features. Learning difficulties do not alone establish formal intellectual disability; early multidomain delay is mapped cautiously.
